questions.prompt: What does a studio need to do during onboarding before it can take payments in Momence?

options.text: Buy a card reader so in-person and online payments both work
Connect its own Stripe account, ideally early in onboarding
Choose a pass-through setting so fee rules are in place first
Sign a separate processing agreement with Momence’s team

questions.reveal: Connecting Stripe is on the onboarding checklist. Doing it early means the studio can take payments sooner.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks whether payment processing adds a second monthly software bill. What do you tell her?

options.text: Yes, but it’s waived for the first months after she signs up
No, Momence absorbs the processing cost on every plan it sells
It’s bundled into the plan price, so there’s no fee on any sale
No second bill; fees are taken per transaction through Stripe

questions.reveal: Processing fees come out of each transaction, as on every booking system, and chargebacks, refunds and PCI compliance are included. There’s no extra processing plan.

questions.prompt: How do recurring memberships get paid in Momence?

options.text: The client’s saved card is charged automatically each billing date
Staff charge each member through point of sale on renewal day
Members get an emailed payment link to pay before each cycle
The studio exports a list and runs the charges inside Stripe

questions.reveal: The card saved at checkout is reused for recurring billing, so the studio doesn’t chase each payment.

questions.prompt: A day spa owner says clients book and don’t show. She doesn’t want to charge in full at booking. What do you show her?

options.text: A reminder sequence that texts clients the day before each visit
Passing card fees on so no-shows at least cover processing costs
Card details taken at booking without a charge, backed by her terms
Request-only appointments so staff approve each booking first

questions.reveal: Saving the card holds the spot without charging it. With a no-show fee in her terms, she can collect it.

questions.prompt: A prospect on Arketa asks, “Can you pass card fees on to clients?” How should you frame it?

options.text: Yes, and it’s something Arketa can’t do, so it’s a reason to switch
Yes, and we recommend every studio turn it on from the first day
Yes, it’s an option she controls; ask if she passes them on today
No, but we can lower her rate later to make up the difference

questions.reveal: Arketa studios can pass fees on too, so it isn’t a differentiator. Her answer tells you how to compare costs.

questions.prompt: Which statement about passing on card fees is accurate to say on a demo?

options.text: Studios can pass on all, part or none of it, on a sliding scale
It’s all or nothing, so clients pay the full fee or none of it
It covers online card payments only, never ACH or in person
It’s only available once the studio adds the marketing suite

questions.reveal: Pass-through is flexible: all fees can go to clients on a sliding scale. Whether members can be exempted is still being confirmed.

questions.prompt: A small-town studio owner says her clients would be upset by a card fee. She’s otherwise keen. What do you do?

options.text: Ask her to try it for a month and count how many clients complain
Explain that most US studios now pass card fees on to clients
Offer to exempt her members so only drop-ins see the card fee
Respect it, leave pass-through off and compare costs without it

questions.reveal: Pass-through is optional, and pushing after she’s said no costs trust. Exempting members isn’t confirmed, so don’t offer it.

questions.prompt: You’re pricing against a prospect’s current costs. She doesn’t pass fees on today. What’s the cleanest comparison?

options.text: Show the plan price alone, since processing is the same anywhere
Compare total cost with fees off, then show passing on as an option
Assume she’ll pass fees on and show savings against her costs
Leave processing out until she asks, then quote a standard rate

questions.reveal: Start from how she runs today, then show what changes if she chooses to pass fees on. Assuming pass-through inflates the savings.

questions.prompt: A prospect says, “Just tell me your card rate. I’m comparing three systems.” What do you do?

options.text: Give the rate from your last demo and say you’ll confirm it later
Say rates stay confidential until she’s ready to sign an agreement
Tell her we match any provider, so the rate won’t be an issue
Give our rates and what they include, then ask what she pays now

questions.reveal: Our rates are confirmed: 3.9% + $0.30 online, 3.7% + $0.05 in person and 1.8% ACH. Her current rate makes the comparison real.

questions.prompt: Late in a strong demo, the prospect says her current card rate is lower than ours and it’s her last holdout. What’s the best move?

options.text: Promise to match her rate so the deal doesn’t stall on processing
Get her current rate in writing and take it to your manager now
Tell her processing costs the same everywhere, so it won’t matter
Suggest passing fees on so the rate stops mattering to her at all

questions.reveal: A rate match needs approval. In one demo the AE got a lower rate approved while the prospect stepped away, which kept the momentum.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks what’s included in Momence’s card processing rates. What’s accurate?

options.text: Chargeback, refund and PCI fees, plus the automatic card updater
Only the Stripe fee; chargebacks and refunds are billed separately
The card reader, which Momence supplies free with every plan
Chargebacks only; PCI compliance is billed as a yearly fee

questions.reveal: Chargeback fees, refund fees, PCI compliance fees and the automatic card updater are all included in the rates.

questions.prompt: A prospect asks if ACH is cheaper than cards, and by how much. What do you say?

options.text: ACH costs the same as cards, so offer whichever clients prefer
ACH is only for paying Momence’s bill, so it doesn’t apply here
ACH is 1.8%, less than a card’s 3.9% + $0.30 online
ACH is free for the studio, so steer every member onto it

questions.reveal: ACH (direct debit) is 1.8%. Online cards are 3.9% + $0.30, so ACH costs the studio less, and it still has a fee.

questions.prompt: Where does an owner first see that membership payments have failed?

options.text: A failed payments tile on the dashboard, with a report behind it
An inbox alert each time Stripe declines a member’s saved card
A weekly summary email sent to the owner from her Stripe account
Only in the sales report, which she has to run by date range

questions.reveal: The dashboard shows failed membership payments when she logs in. The report shows who paid later and who still owes.

questions.prompt: An owner asks, “How many times will the system retry a failed card?” What do you say?

options.text: Two or three times, then it stops and the client loses access
Unlimited times, until the client updates the card on file
It reruns automatically; you’ll confirm the exact number
It doesn’t retry, so staff rerun each charge by hand

questions.reveal: Reruns show on screen with the next rerun date. The retry count is being confirmed, and one AE guessed it on a call.

questions.prompt: What can the studio edit to control what clients hear about a failed payment?

options.text: The pass-through setting on that client’s membership
The transactional email templates for failed payments
The sequence that runs before each membership renews
The Stripe receipt that goes out after every charge

questions.reveal: Transactional templates cover failed and retried payments, and the studio can change the wording.

questions.prompt: A dance studio owner runs the door alone before class and needs walk-ins paid fast. What do you show first?

options.text: The online checkout, so walk-ins book on their phones at the door
The marketing suite, so walk-ins become leads after the visit
The free app, so walk-ins download it and buy a class pack
Check-in from the class page and payment through point of sale

questions.reveal: Lead with the flow he named as his priority. In one demo this came 20 minutes in, after features he didn’t ask about.

questions.prompt: A prospect leaving WellnessLiving asks if her members’ recurring cards will transfer. What’s the best answer?

options.text: Her data comes over; cards depend on what WellnessLiving releases
Yes, every card transfers, since onboarding handles the migration
No, cards never transfer, so plan to collect every one again
Cards transfer only if she pays an exit fee to Momence’s team

questions.reveal: Momence’s team pulls the data, but the old provider controls the card file. Don’t promise every card.

questions.prompt: When a MindBody studio wants its members’ saved cards moved, what usually has to happen?

options.text: Members re-enter their cards in the Momence app before go-live
The studio requests MindBody’s card file, which MindBody charges for
Momence’s team exports the cards from MindBody at no cost to anyone
Stripe moves the cards on its own once the account is connected

questions.reveal: MindBody charges for the exit file with payment profiles. The card-export fee depends on the software and is about $500.

questions.prompt: You’re scoping a switch. Which question tells you most about how much stored cards matter for this studio?

options.text: How long they’ve been on their current booking system
Which payment methods their clients use most often
How many members pay on recurring cards right now
Whether they pass card fees on to clients today

questions.reveal: Cards matter for recurring billing. A studio with mostly class packs has less to move, and some owners only want the client list.

questions.prompt: Which of these payment facts is confirmed and safe to state on a demo?

options.text: Members can be exempted from pass-through with a setting
Failed cards are retried exactly three times, then stop
Studios can accept HSA cards by switching them on in setup
Clients can pay by ACH at 1.8%, less than a card costs

questions.reveal: ACH at 1.8% is confirmed. Member exemptions, the retry count and HSA cards are still being confirmed, so say “let me confirm that.”
